newsitem.title: USA: Tom Brown increases offer to buy Presidio.
newsitem.headline: Tom Brown increases offer to buy Presidio.

text.p: Tom Brown Inc., an independent oil and gas company, said Friday it has agreed to increase its bid for Presidio Oil Co. to about $193 million from $183 million to gain support of the bankrupt company's creditors.
Tom Brown, based in Midland, Texas, said it would also assume certain Presidio liabilities.

Presidio had agreed to the merger before it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in August. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.
Among Presidio's top creditors are U.S. Trust Co. Texas, U.S. Trust Co. New York, Bank of Montreal Trust Co., Chase Manhattan Corp. and NationsBank Corp.
The new offer consists of about $105 million cash and about 5.35 million Tom Brown shares worth $16.50 each, it said.
Tom Brown said that in exchange for the increased bid, all impaired creditor classes have agreed to support Presidio's reorganization plan.

"The company increased its offer from $183 million to $193.1 million to gain consent of the creditors," Tom Brown Chairman Donald Evans said in a statement. "The higher price reflects the improved gas market and higher natural gas prices currently existing in the Rocky Mountains."
Evans said the proposed acquisition is now in the final stage.
Tom Brown's stock fell 37.5 cents to $17.25 on Nasdaq. Presidio edged up 1 cent to 3 cents on the Nasdaq bulletin board.
